title: I Followed the After-Hours Alarm Bypass Through Three Floors After They Cut Security

parts.text: They cut the night guard and posted a bypass code on the third-floor printer. I was thirty-five, facilities contractor, holding a badge that still opened one stairwell. At 10:22 p.m. the code opened floor three and, I found, the stair door to four. Temporary, the vendor said. I photographed the printer page, both doors, the time. Then a delivery driver I did not recognize used the same numbers behind me, waving a bag of burritos like a credential. The burritos were not a credential.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The burrito driver just used the printer code toward floor four.

social.video_title: They replaced a guard with a printer code that opened two floors — Part 1/3
social.description: Night, cut security, burritos as a badge. Would you have let the stair door close?

parts.text: I closed the stair and called the after-hours vendor. They said morning. I ticketed it at 10:26, then walked to five because the leak I was hired for was five. The code opened five. Three floors, one printer, zero guard. I sat with the leak. At 10:50 the driver was at the loading-dock keypad trying combinations. The dock camera still worked because the old guard had fought for it. I sent the still to the morning ticket and cc'd workplace safety.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He is on the dock keypad; safety now has the still.

social.video_title: The printer code opened five and he tried the dock — Part 2/3
social.description: Leak as witness, three floors, a camera a fired guard loved. Would you have gone home?

parts.text: Morning was a vendor meeting. The printer page came down. Codes rotated. They hired a walking guard again, not the same one, because companies rarely uncut the person who was right. I kept the leak work order. The driver was trespassed. Safety sent a note about not printing codes. I replied all with the 10:26 ticket and nothing else. Nights need legs. I badge one floor at a time. Burritos stay in lobbies. Printers print invoices, not buildings.

social.video_title: The printer page came down and walking came back — Part 3/3
social.description: Rotated codes, trespass, a ticket as the whole reply. Was a burrito a guard?
